  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Failed job-log fetches append a placeholder to `LOG_FILES`, so fingerprinting treats unavailable logs as evidence and can assign unrelated failures the same generic signature instead of using the source-keyed fallback.
  WHY: Reports with different escalated items can share a workflow and failing step and consequently consume the same lineage; severity differed, with OpenAI rating it MAJOR and GLM rating it NIT, so the higher severity is used.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:721, 767-784; scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2905-2924 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new fingerprint does not match existing heal issues with the old label-only fingerprint, and label reports do not pass a `source_key` to provide an alternate match.
  WHY: A repeat report for an item with an existing open heal issue can open a duplicate issue, while a closed prior issue will not contribute to that item's lineage.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:721 | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Run-less `workflow_run` reports without an issue number use `none` in the source-keyed signature, so distinct failures for the same label and repository can share a fingerprint.
  WHY: Distinct release-blocker failures can be lumped into one lineage and capped based on previous unrelated failures.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:707 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `tracking_issue` is passed to run selection for both issue-kind and pull-request-kind escalation reports, so a PR number matching a tracking issue number can select that tracking issue's validation runs.
  WHY: Label-escalation reports skip the run-binding gate, allowing misattributed tracking-issue logs to be used as the PR's failure evidence.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:578-584, 715-721 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The per-item fingerprint claim overstates the fallback's scope because reports with linked runs whose logs cannot be read retain the error-signature path.
  WHY: This pre-existing logs-unavailable case can still give distinct escalated items the same `no-error-lines` fingerprint; GLM assesses it as not made worse by the diff and identifies the PR description as over-promising.

- File: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh
  Line: 713-721
  PROBLEM: The script relies on the presence of entries in the LOG_FILES variable (populated by a fetcher) to determine if logs are readable, but the fetcher appends placeholder strings (e.g., "(job log unavailable)") to this list even when a fetch fails.
  WHY: The signature generation incorrectly treats failed log fetches as successful, which can cause unrelated failures to share a lineage if their log-fetch failures produce identical placeholders.
- File: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh

The new signature `label:${LABEL:-unknown}|source:${SOURCE_REPO}#${ISSUE_NUMBER:-none}` uses `none` as a fallback for the issue number, causing all such run-less reports for the same label in the same repository to share a fingerprint.
  WHY: Distinct release-blocker failures can be lumped into a single heal lineage, causing a distinct, new failure to be erroneously capped by the lineage limit based on previous unrelated failures.
- TASK_GAP

  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh
  Evidence of absence: The signature logic `SIGNATURE="label:${LABEL:-unknown}|source:${SOURCE_REPO}#${ISSUE_NUMBER:-none}"` uses `none` for run-less reports that lack an issue number. This causes different `workflow_run` failures (which are distinct escalated items) to share the same fingerprint component within a repository, failing the intent that run-less reports from "different issues" never share one lineage.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh
  Line or code reference: 578-584, 705-710
  PROBLEM: A failed job-log fetch writes `(job log unavailable)` to `FILTERED_LOG` and appends it to `LOG_FILES`. The fingerprint branch therefore treats it as available log evidence instead of using the new source-keyed fallback.
  WHY: `error_signature` returns `no-error-lines` for this placeholder. Reports from different escalated items that share a workflow and failing step consequently get the same fingerprint, so unrelated failures can still consume the same lineage and trigger a false lineage-cap escalation.

  WHY: On a repeated report for an item with an existing open heal issue from before this change, the new fingerprint will not match that issue. The intake can open a duplicate heal issue rather than deduplicating against the existing one; a closed prior issue also will not contribute to the item's existing lineage.

  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- File: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py
  Line or code reference: build_issue_payload, line 707 (`tracking_issue=_positive_int(issue.get("number"))`), applied unconditionally for both kind="issue" and kind="pull_request" (pull_request path confirmed by tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:5737)
  PROBLEM: GitHub shares one number space between issues and PRs, so PR #249 and tracking issue #249 both exist in a repo. The new tracking-title match now also fires for PR-kind escalation reports: a PR carrying an escalation label whose number equals an orchestrator project's tracking issue number will link that project's failed `AI Validate [tracking:<N>]` runs even though they belong to the tracking issue, not the PR. Label-escalation reports skip the intake's run-binding gate (agents.md: "Label-escalation issue and pull_request reports are outside this gate"), so nothing downstream rejects the misattributed runs; their logs are fetched and fed to diagnosis as the PR's failure evidence.
  WHY: a `ai:harness-broken` escalation on PR #249 of a repo whose tracking issue #249 just failed validation attaches the tracking issue's validation-run logs to the PR's heal report; the intake then fingerprints and diagnoses from the wrong failure evidence, and the reporter's "picks the failed runs that belong to it" contract (workflow_failure_heal_report.sh header, line updated by this PR) is violated for PR-kind reports.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh (line 721) and scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py (budget_decision, lines 2905-2924, 782-784 of the intake)
  Line or code reference: the new `label:<label>|source:<repo>#<n>` signature vs. existing open heal issues filed with the old label-only fingerprint; label reports pass no `--source-key` (intake lines 782-784 covers only autofix_failure/phase_failure), so `source_duplicate` (heal.py 2911-2912) can never match for label reports.
  PROBLEM: The fingerprint format change orphans in-flight lineages. A run-less repeat report for an item that already has an OPEN pre-fix heal issue (filed under the shared old fingerprint) matches nothing: `duplicate` requires the new fp, `source_duplicate` requires a source_key label reports never carry. The intake therefore opens a second open heal issue for the same escalated item at gen 1 while the old one is still open, instead of the pre-fix behavior (action=duplicate, no new issue). Each affected item costs one duplicate diagnosis run and possibly a parallel fix PR against the same area; duplicates also consume the `WORKFLOW_HEAL_MAX_OPEN_ISSUES` open-issue budget. The new test only exercises the closed-issue case (tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:2197 uses state="closed"), so the open-heal-issue transition is unverified. Same class applies to run-less workflow_run reports whose old `label:unknown` fingerprint heal issues are open.
  WHY: item X re-fails run-less after the release while its pre-fix open heal issue is still open; the intake files a duplicate gen-1 heal issue and runs a second full diagnosis.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 578-584 (failed fetch writes the `(job log unavailable)` placeholder and still appends it to LOG_FILES for non-phase kinds) vs. the new else branch at 715-721, reached only when `LOG_FILES` is empty (line 705).
  PROBLEM: The else branch fires only for reports that linked no run at all (or no failed jobs found). A label report that linked runs whose every job-log fetch failed still takes the line 705 branch and gets the generic `no-error-lines` signature, so it is not keyed per escalated item. The PR description states "a report with no readable run logs ... is fingerprinted on label:<label>|source:<repo>#<n>", which does not hold for that sub-case; README (the shipped doc) is accurate ("still links no run") and the added code comment ("No run to read") is accurate, but the boundary is unstated anywhere a future reader would check first.
  WHY: two different escalated items in one repo, each with one linked run whose log archive is unavailable, share the same `no-error-lines` fingerprint and one lineage; a third distinct failure on either item can escalate at the lineage cap instead of filing its own heal issue. This is pre-existing behavior for the logs-unavailable case and not made worse by the diff, but the new per-item fingerprint claim over-promises in the PR description.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash
